skill.name: github-release-management
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub releases with version planning, changelog generation, CI validation, package publishing, rollback workflows, and AI swarm task delegation.
skill.summary: Plan, validate, publish, and monitor GitHub releases with AI-assisted orchestration.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown release-automation guide with many static false positives from code fences. Real risks remain in shell command substitutions, predictable /tmp files, GitHub and npm token handling, and credentialed publish/deploy workflows.

remediation.issue: Credentialed publishing is shown as a direct workflow step.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit human approval gates, protected environments, least-privilege tokens, and dry-run defaults before npm publish, Docker push, or release deployment commands.
Use npm trusted publishing or temporary per-step configuration, then delete .npmrc and prevent it from entering caches, artifacts, or logs.

remediation.issue: Release metadata is stored in predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or CI-provided temporary directories and restrict file permissions for generated PR, commit, and changelog data.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitutions are used in release commands.
remediation.suggestion: Quote derived values, validate tags and versions, and prefer structured files or GitHub Actions outputs over inline shell interpolation.

content.value_statement: Release work often spans versioning, testing, changelogs, artifacts, and deployment checks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured release workflow.
actual_capabilities: Draft GitHub releases with generated notes and target branches.
Plan semantic version changes from commits, pull requests, and release labels.
Coordinate validation tasks for tests, builds, security checks, and compatibility checks.
Generate changelog, release notes, migration guide, and announcement drafts.
Describe GitHub Actions workflows for release, hotfix, artifact upload, and monitoring.
Outline rollback and post-release monitoring procedures.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, and project-specific package tooling.
Publishing and deployment commands need valid credentials and human approval.
Examples must be adapted before use in repositories with different release policies.
The skill provides orchestration guidance, not a verified release system by itself.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Standard Release
use_cases.description: Create a release branch, update version files, generate notes, run validation, and open a release pull request.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Enterprise Release Checks
use_cases.description: Plan staged deployment, artifact generation, security scanning, approvals, monitoring, and rollback criteria.

use_cases.title: Handle an Emergency Hotfix
use_cases.description: Draft a hotfix workflow with critical tests, release creation, communication steps, and post-release monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Release Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GitHub release for version [version]. Include version files, changelog tasks, validation checks, release notes, and approval steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the merged pull requests and commits since [previous tag] to draft release notes for [version]. Highlight breaking changes and migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions release workflow for [project]. Include tests, build artifacts, security checks, package publishing, and rollback safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Repository Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a coordinated release across [repositories]. Include dependency order, compatibility checks, tags, artifacts, deployment windows, and rollback ownership.

output_examples.input: Plan release v2.0.0 for a Node package.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering branch creation, version bump, changelog draft, test and build validation, release pull request, npm publish approval, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Create release notes from merged pull requests.
output_examples.output: Categorized release notes with features, fixes, breaking changes, contributors, migration guidance, and known issues.
A focused hotfix plan with branch source, cherry-pick steps, critical tests, approval gate, publication steps, announcement, and rollback checks.

best_practices: Require human approval before publishing packages, pushing images, or deploying production releases.
Run release commands in isolated CI jobs with least-privilege tokens and protected environments.
Review generated changelogs and release notes before using them in public releases.
anti_patterns: Do not run publish, deploy, or rollback commands from unreviewed AI output.
Do not store registry tokens in files that may enter caches, logs, or artifacts.
Do not use emergency release paths to skip required security or compliance checks.

faq.question: Does this skill publish releases automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflow patterns. You should require approval before any publish or deployment command runs.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, npm or yarn, and optionally Claude Flow or swarm tooling.

faq.question: Can it generate changelogs?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to collect pull requests and commits, then draft categorized changelogs and migration notes.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes multi-package and multi-repository release coordination patterns.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use CI secret stores, least-privilege tokens, protected environments, and cleanup steps for temporary credential files.

faq.question: Is it safe for production releases?
faq.answer: It can support production workflows when commands, credentials, approvals, and rollback steps are reviewed by maintainers.
